title: Relationships & Joins
description: Define relationships between tables (one-to-many, many-to-many) and query related data.

slides.title: One-to-Many Relationship
slides.content:
# User → Posts

A user can have many posts. Define:
- A `ForeignKey` in the child table (`post.user_id`).
- A `relationship()` in the parent to access children.

```python
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    posts = relationship("Post", back_populates="author")

class Post(Base):
    __tablename__ = "posts"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"))
    author = relationship("User", back_populates="posts")
```

slides.title: Full Example
slides.content: Create the models and use them.
slides.codeSnippet:
class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    posts = relationship("Post", back_populates="user", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

class Post(Base):
    __tablename__ = "posts"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = Column(String)
    user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"))
    user = relationship("User", back_populates="posts")

quizData.question: What does `ForeignKey("users.id")` do?

options.text: It creates a new column that references the users table
It deletes the user when a post is deleted

quizData.explanation: ForeignKey defines a column that references the primary key of another table, establishing a link.

slides.title: Querying with Joins
slides.content:
# Fetch Related Data

Use `select(...).join(...)` to load related data in one query.

```python
# Get user with their posts
stmt = select(User).where(User.id == user_id).options(selectinload(User.posts))
result = await session.execute(stmt)
user = result.scalar_one()
```

`selectinload` loads the posts in a separate query (efficient).
`joinedload` uses a SQL JOIN.

slides.title: Loading Relationships
slides.content: Fetch a user and all their posts.
slides.codeSnippet:
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload

async def get_user_with_posts(db: AsyncSession, user_id: int):
    stmt = select(User).where(User.id == user_id).options(selectinload(User.posts))
    result = await db.execute(stmt)
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()

slides.title: Many-to-Many Relationships
slides.content:
# Student ↔ Course

Many-to-many uses an association table.

```python
student_course = Table(
    "student_course",
    Base.metadata,
    Column("student_id", ForeignKey("students.id"), primary_key=True),
    Column("course_id", ForeignKey("courses.id"), primary_key=True)
)

class Student(Base):
    __tablename__ = "students"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    courses = relationship("Course", secondary=student_course, back_populates="students")

class Course(Base):
    __tablename__ = "courses"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    students = relationship("Student", secondary=student_course, back_populates="courses")
```

slides.title: Many-to-Many Example
slides.codeSnippet:
# Add a course to a student
student = await get_student(db, student_id)
course = await get_course(db, course_id)
student.courses.append(course)
await db.commit()

# Fetch student with courses
stmt = select(Student).where(Student.id == student_id).options(selectinload(Student.courses))
result = await db.execute(stmt)
student = result.scalar_one()

quizData.question: What is the `secondary` argument in a `relationship()` used for?

options.text: It specifies the foreign key column
It names the association table for many-to-many
It defines the order of loading

quizData.explanation: In many-to-many, `secondary` points to the association table that links the two main tables.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Always use `selectinload` for collections when possible. It loads all related objects in a second query, which is often faster than `joinedload` for many items.
